Local BJP leader Parappil Balakrishnan surrendered and lookout notices remain against five accused abroad, per Press Trust of India.
items.title: Kerala Police Name Two More Accused in Rs 8 Crore Qatar Theft

items.summary:
The Centre told the Calcutta High Court that four Nicobarese tribal representatives are “not necessary or proper parties” to a case challenging forest rights recognition on Great Nicobar Island, which cleared the way for its ₹81,000-crore development project. In an affidavit seen by Hindustan Times, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs said the applicants bypassed statutory remedies and approached the court after nearly four years’ delay. The tribal representatives allege no Gram Sabha consent was obtained before land diversion. The next hearing is scheduled for November 25 and 26.

items.summary: Semafor announces a live event titled 'The Next 3 Billion On Tour,' scheduled to begin at 3:00 p.m. SAST, focusing on financial inclusion in South Africa as an established model for economic opportunity through instant payments, digital banking, and open finance. The program convenes policymakers, business leaders, and innovators to explore how financial access drives inclusive growth across Africa and beyond, with lessons applicable regionally and internationally; attendees are invited to check back after the event for highlights.
items.title: Semafor Hosts Financial Inclusion Event on Africa's Next Billion Users

items.summary: Punjab National Bank said it settled three customer claims totalling Rs 43 lakh over alleged financial irregularities at its Greater Noida branch, and assured account holders that genuine claims would be honoured. The statement follows complaints alleging more than Rs 11. 24 crore was taken from savings accounts and fixed deposits across 21 listed account holders, with two customers reporting losses above Rs 1 crore each; local account holders put the suspected fraud at around Rs 35 crore.
items.title: PNB Settles Rs 43 Lakh in Greater Noida Branch Claims

items.summary: On October 29, 2026, a StockEdge technical scan found that seven stocks in the Nifty200 pack had closing prices crossing above their 200-day moving averages. The 200-day DMA is used by traders as a key indicator of overall trend; when price stays above it on the daily timeframe, the stock is generally read as being in an uptrend.
items.title: Seven Nifty200 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary: The Orissa high court issued notices to five suspended Biju Janata Dal (BJD) MLAs, directing replies by December 4. The party alleged eight of its members voted for BJP-backed independent Dilip Ray over joint nominee Datteswar Hota in the March 16 Rajya Sabha poll; both received 23 first preference votes each.
items.title: Orissa High Court Notices BJD MLAs Over Cross-Voting Allegations

items.summary: The review opens by noting the title is taken too seriously, describing a couple whose marriage has soured. It explains that Manjula and Kannan are drawn into a cosmic game involving a sorcerer and time travel that returns them to their younger selves with old tensions intact. The reviewer finds the eight-episode series lengthy and repetitive but entertaining in its college scenes.
items.title: Review of Love Always Tamil series on JioHotstar

items.summary: Police in Jammu and Kashmir arrested 10 overground workers in the Shopian terror financing case, officials said on Friday. The arrests followed an investigation into suspicious online transactions across multiple payment platforms that traced money trails linked to terrorists jailed elsewhere. Officials described it as a significant breakthrough against the terror ecosystem.
items.title: J&K Police Arrest 10 in Shopian Terror Financing Case

items.summary: Democratic Republic of Congo President Felix Tshisekedi called on Russia to support a UN-backed resolution demanding the withdrawal of Rwandan troops from eastern Congo. Speaking at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, he reaffirmed his commitment to diplomatic efforts through Washington and Doha processes. The appeal follows US sanctions on entities accused of supporting M23 rebels, with no immediate response from Rwanda.
items.title: DR Congo Leader Appeals for Russian Backing on Rwandan Troop Withdrawal

items.summary: India's advance-to-decline ratio fell to 0.9 in October, its lowest since March 2026, signalling declining stocks outnumbered advancing ones. While Sensex and Nifty rose 2.3% and 1.4%, the BSE MidCap 150 and SmallCap 250 declined 3% and 4.2%. Profit-booking, stretched valuations and institutional rotation toward large caps weigh on sentiment; Tejas Shah of Equirus Securities said investors grew more selective.
items.title: Market Breadth Weakens as Advance-Decline Ratio Hits Seven-Month Low

items.summary: Computer Age Management Services Ltd reported a consolidated profit after tax of ₹131.49 crore for the second quarter of fiscal 2026-27, up 14.4 per cent year-on-year, on October 29, 2026. The board recommended an interim dividend of ₹3.25 per share. Operating revenue rose 10.0 per cent to ₹414.47 crore and EBITDA reached ₹190.86 crore, up 13.5 per cent. Managing Director Anuj Kumar said the quarter showed strength in CAMS's platform-led model and diversification strategy. The story is based on company exchange filings for informational purposes only.
items.title: CAMS Reports Profit Rise and Announces Interim Dividend in Q2 FY27

items.summary: Punjab National Bank assured customers on Thursday that all genuine claims would be honoured after allegations of financial irregularities involving savings accounts and fixed deposits at its Greater Noida branch. The bank said it had settled three customer claims totalling ₹43 lakh as of Wednesday, while account holders allege nearly ₹35 crore went missing from their deposits. Police suspended several employees, including the branch manager, and registered a case; PNB has not yet assessed the total irregularities or affected accounts.
items.title: PNB Settles ₹43 Lakh In Claims In ₹35 Crore Greater Noida Fraud Case

items.summary: The Election Commission of India extended the State Internal Revision (SIR) deadline for Maharashtra, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana and Nagaland. The final voter lists will be published on November 30 for five states and December 22 for Delhi. Objection deadlines were also pushed back from October dates to late November or mid-December.
items.title: Election Commission extends SIR deadlines across six states and Delhi

items.summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) wrote to Sonia Gandhi asking that the opposition INDIA bloc's planned November 1 mega-rally at Ramlila Maidan be postponed past Diwali. In a letter, CTI urged rescheduling to after November 10 or moving it to Burari Maidan. The body said traffic restrictions and heavy footfall could worsen losses traders already face during the festive season, when trade worth around Rs 25,000 crore is estimated across Delhi's markets between Dhanteras and Diwali. CTI Chairman Brijesh Goyal stressed that business owners are facing widespread panic, clarifying their plea is about survival rather than political opposition. Traders said November 1 is the busiest single day for festive inventory transit.
items.title: Delhi traders urge Gandhi to postpone INDIA bloc rally

items.summary: In an editorial, The Guardian argues that although ten years have passed since the referendum, Britain’s Brexit debate has changed because of Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine and Donald Trump’s presidency. It holds that a reappraisal is now warranted, noting the prime minister called for open discussion at the Labour conference last month. Kemi Badenoch rejects this, accusing the government of stirring division; The Guardian calls her position disingenuous.
items.title: Guardian editorial says Kemi Badenoch is trapped in Brexit denial

items.summary: The UK government gave engine-maker Rolls-Royce £1. 25bn to part-fund a next-generation single-aisle aircraft engine, the UltraFan, buried briefly in the chancellor's speech amid talk of rising debt interest. The company sits fifth in the FTSE 100 with a market value of £105bn and can spend up to £9bn on buy-backs this year. Chief executive Tufan Erginbilgiç had earlier said he would “appreciate” government support, seen as implying rivals elsewhere might pay if the UK did not. The subsidy funds part of a joint 10-year £2.
items.title: UK Subsidises Rolls-Royce UltraFan Engine Development

items.summary: Tourism and hospitality leaders across Devon and Cornwall reacted to chancellor John Healey's first Budget, describing it as offering both support and pressure. Sue Jewell of the South East Cornwall Tourism Association said it 'gave with one hand and took with the other', noting staff cuts after a legal minimum wage rise of 3.9% in April. Toby Parkins predicted about 900 extra businesses would benefit from higher business-rate thresholds, while Helen Wylde-Archibald welcomed stability but flagged weak growth support for farming and food. James Kittow said the sector felt forgotten amid unchanged inheritance tax on inherited assets over £2.5m worth facing 20% tax since April.
items.title: South West leaders weigh in on Budget's mixed message for tourism and business

items.summary: The US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3. 75%-4% in a decision made within a week of the midterm elections, following its first rate rise in three years at the September meeting. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the monetary policy was starting to work while inflation remained above target and economic growth accelerated. Figures published after the announcement showed the economy growing by 3. 4% on an annualised basis in the three months to September, stronger than expected, with personal spending up 3. 8% and private investment rising 19. 4%. Inflation increased by 3. 7% over the year to September. The vote was not unanimous: while 10 of the 12 committee members supported holding rates, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for an increase to 4%-4. 25%. Warsh declined to forecast future moves, noting more data would emerge before the next meeting on 8-9 December.
items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady as US Economy Grows

items.summary: New data showed the US economy grew faster than expected this summer, but analysts said the strong reading before next week's midterm elections is unlikely to cheer voters worried about rising inflation. A Republican strategist told Bloomberg that 'voters don't vote on GDP,' while Navy Federal Credit Union's chief economist noted strain as consumers spend more than they earn.
items.title: US Economy Grows Faster Than Expected Amid Inflation Concerns

items.summary: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week, killing one person and wounding seven including a child, has admitted targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African. Prosecutors said he made this admission on Thursday.
items.title: French Suspect Admits Targeting Muslims and Africans in Paris Shooting

items.summary: A sole arbitrator dismissed Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited's ₹12.08 crore claim against Goldi Solar Limited and directed BHEL to pay ₹4 crore in compensation, plus interest and costs. The award was delivered on October 14, 2026 by Justice V. Jagannathan at the Arbitration & Conciliation Centre in Bengaluru. The Tribunal found multiple contractual violations by BHEL after examining evidence from both parties.
items.title: Arbiter Orders BHEL To Compensate Goldi Solar

items.summary: On October 29, 2026, TOYO Co., Ltd., a Japanese solar manufacturer with facilities in Ethiopia and Humble, Texas, announced that U.S. Customs and Border Protection released shipments of its Ethiopian-made solar cells after reviewing supply chain documentation. The company submitted records showing traceability of polysilicon and wafers sourcing and stated it cooperated fully throughout the process.
items.title: TOYO Secures U.S. Customs Release of Ethiopian Solar Cells After Supply Chain Review

items.summary: Iraq's culture ministry says the former Baghdad home of novelist Agatha Christie has been left to decay over more than a century. The padlocked, dilapidated heritage property sits on the Tigris River and the government says it will make it available to anyone willing to restore it. A $200 electricity bill was found in its door this month. Christie visited Iraq many times; she met her husband Max Mallowan there in 1930, and wrote novels set in the country.
items.title: Baghdad's abandoned Agatha Christie home waits for a restorer

items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance is investigating a potential security breach involving up to $5.8 billion in digital assets, which could become the largest cryptocurrency hack in history if confirmed. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze more than $2.3 billion in associated assets. Binance stated user funds are safe while warning of scams; founder CZ said he no longer manages the exchange. Blockchain analysis tracks about $5.78 billion across wallets, though this is not a confirmed theft amount. The story remains developing as Binance has not yet confirmed whether transfers were unauthorized or how the breach occurred.
items.title: Binance Investigates Possible $5.8 Billion Crypto Hack

items.summary: As the COP31 summit approaches, Carbon Brief asked six experts what they expect from China and which signals to watch. Responses emphasize multilateralism, trade tensions over clean technologies, and implementation of existing targets. One expert noted that after vice-premier Ding Xuexiang shared at COP29 that China has provided and mobilised over 177bn yuan ($26.5bn) in climate finance for developing countries since 2016, Beijing has issued no further quantitative updates while urging developed nations to lead on finance. Others flagged the $300bn climate finance goal as a key focus. Experts also expect China to push trade perspectives into negotiations and remain reluctant to link electrification targets to fossil-fuel phaseouts.
items.title: Experts weigh in on China's COP31 climate priorities

items.summary: India's Ministry of Finance raised its growth forecast for fiscal year FY27 (April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027) to 7.3% from the previous estimate of 7.1%, citing a reassessment in its October economic review. The ministry flagged inflationary pressure and rupee weakness driven by El Nino, oil prices and global uncertainties, while pointing to foreign exchange reserves worth some $721 billion as support for sustaining expansion.
items.title: India Raises Fiscal Growth Forecast Amid Inflation and Rupee Pressure

items.summary: On Oct 30, Foxconn chairman Young Liu told reporters at the company's annual technology event that a collaboration with US developer OpenAI was in progress after he met chief executive Sam Altman earlier. Details were limited; any deal would build on a 2025 agreement to co-develop AI hardware. Liu said the industry is not in a bubble and Foxconn expects double-digit growth in 2027, while separately noting humanoid robot deployments at its Houston plant.
items.title: Foxconn signals OpenAI partnership, dismisses AI bubble fears

items.summary: French business school Insead announced on Oct 30 that it has launched the Research Lab for Human and Organisational Thriving, funded with US$3 million from Google.org and S$3.83 million overall backing tied to $3.8 million reported in its headline. Winnie Jiang will serve as academic director. The lab studies how AI affects human connectivity, meaning and well-being at work and life.
items.title: Insead Launches AI Research Lab With Google Backing

items.summary: The Indicator newsletter highlights two risks Anthropic flagged in its IPO prospectus, which ran about 94 pages. The first is that advanced semiconductor manufacturing concentrates heavily in Taiwan, so a disruption there could affect the whole AI economy. The second risk concerns aging technology: because companies lock into pricey contracts for software and GPUs while hardware improves quickly, firms like Anthropic may pay premiums for older equipment even as competitors do more for less.
items.title: Anthropic's S-1 Reveals Two Business Risks

items.summary: Shares of Reddit fell 23 per cent in premarket trading after the company warned that Google's increasing use of AI search could reduce referral traffic and shrink its user base, citing fresh evidence of AI-driven disruption. Total daily active unique visitors may drop by a low double-digit percentage from about 130 million if referral traffic continues to decline. Analysts note an appropriate reset in expectations amid a clouded near-term outlook.
items.title: Reddit Shares Plunge on Google AI Search Traffic Concerns

items.summary: Intel shares fell 25 per cent in premarket trading after the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $17.07 billion, and warned PC weakness would persist through at least mid-2027. The outlook put Intel on track to lose more than $123 billion in market value. Semiconductor stocks broadly declined as well.
items.title: Intel's weak outlook triggers broad chip selloff

items.summary: China dismissed a report alleging that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted in a spy plot, calling the claims groundless speculation. A New York Times report said US intelligence found a senior Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data centre delivering information to Beijing and monitoring her for steering AI chips to China. Both Nvidia and China's Foreign Ministry denied the allegations.
items.title: China Rejects Report of Spy Plot Targeting Nvidia's Jensen Huang

items.summary: The article examines whether Elon Musk wields political influence comparable to historical American figures, citing his $400 million in Republican donations and SpaceX restrictions on Ukraine. Historian David Nasaw argues billionaires like Musk exercise undue power, while Richard White contends Musk pales beside J.P. Morgan of the Gilded Age. H.W. Brands frames the debate as tensions between democracy and capitalism, suggesting reform may follow Trump's terms. The piece presents these views without independent verification, noting NPR received no reply from Musk.
items.title: Historians Debate Elon Musk's Political Influence Versus Past Moguls

items.summary: Cursor flagged a modified version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension containing malware that could have stolen personal data and granted remote computer access to hackers. Cursor temporarily closed its marketplace on October 30, 2026, after working with service providers to remove the threat; it stated no ongoing risk remains and urged users to install update 2.1.314.
items.title: Security Alert Over Malicious Claude Code Extension Affecting Up To 5,000 Users

items.summary: Uzbekistan introduced Apple Pay and Google Pay for locally issued Visa and Mastercard cards on 27 October, following personal data law amendments in March 2026. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan told Euronews that work is underway to extend the services to domestic Uzcard and HUMO networks, though no timetable has been provided. Head Saida Mirziyoyeva linked the rollout to broader opportunities for international payment systems.
items.title: Apple Pay and Google Pay Launch in Uzbekistan Amid Fintech Reforms

items.summary: US artificial intelligence firms are expanding in the Gulf, a sign that some companies are not shying away despite increased risks to digital infrastructure. Oracle plans to build more data centers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE to meet rising demand, The National reported. Snowflake projects it will invest $300 million in the kingdom through 2030; its customers there include dairy company Almarai and PIF-backed developer Red Sea Global. So far, data center construction has “barely moved the needle for Gulf economies,” according to Bloomberg economist Ziad Daoud.
items.title: Oracle Joins Wave of AI Firms Expanding Data Infrastructure Across the Gulf

items.summary: Microsoft raised $25 billion Thursday in its first bond offering since 2017, citing protection of its AAA credit rating — one of only two left in Corporate America. Its 10-year bonds cost just 5.6%, close to US government borrowing rates. The article contrasts this with lower-rated AI-sector issuers like SpaceX and CoreWeave demanding much higher yields.
items.title: Microsoft's AAA Rating Lets It Borrow at Near-Government Rates Amid AI Debt Fears

items.summary: The IMF says weather events, including a super El Niño, remain an important downside risk for India’s growth. It notes worse-than-expected weather could lower crop yields and weigh on rural activity or push up food prices, but stresses these risks have not yet materialized and are forward-looking only. The Fund also urges the RBI to let the rupee move freely amid energy shocks rather than prop it up.
items.title: IMF Warns El Niño Threatens India Growth, Urges Free Rupee

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has asked banks to strengthen cybersecurity measures and prove compliance with existing rules as attacks on financial institutions rise, Reuters reported. Sources say the RBI also wants checks on API security gaps and information on AI-related risks. The move follows recent incidents in India's banking sector, including a State Bank data leak affecting about 3,900 customers and losses of around $2 million by two non-bank lenders after more than 700 unauthorised transfers from ICICI Bank accounts.
items.title: RBI Presses Banks for Cybersecurity Compliance Amid Rising Attacks

items.summary: Muhammed Riswan, a freestyle footballer from Kerala, won recognition at Instagram's Rings Award 2026 after his November 18, 2023 video of kicking a football toward Keralamkundu Waterfall in Malappuram district went viral. The clip, filmed with friends as casual fun, reportedly crossed 600 million views and earlier earned Guinness World Records recognition on January 8, 2024 for the most-viewed Instagram Reel at that time. Instagram described him as a Kerala footballer whose gravity-defying skills have taken him from local pitches to a global stage. He is one of two Indian winners among 25 selected creators worldwide.
items.title: Kerala freestyle footballer wins Instagram Rings Award for viral waterfall kick

items.summary: Microsoft says it has fixed Always On VPN connection failures triggered by the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates. The company had earlier mistakenly marked the problem resolved in October's cumulative update, then acknowledged it via a late-September service alert for IT administrators. A preview KB5127936 update now addresses the issue; admins can also switch from automatic protocol selection to SSTP or IKEv2 only as a temporary workaround.
items.title: Microsoft Resolves Always On VPN Failures From September Windows Updates

items.summary: The Supreme Court, in suo motu proceedings arising from an elderly couple allegedly losing ₹1.05 crore to fraudsters using forged judicial orders, urged the Reserve Bank of India on Thursday to introduce regulations holding banks accountable when inadequate safeguards contribute to customer losses from digital arrest scams and cyber fraud. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant said compensation should cover at least the amount lost. Appearing for the RBI, Attorney General R Venkataramani said complaints had declined by approximately 50% and requested time to implement a framework by Dec 31.
items.title: Supreme Court Urges RBI To Compensate Digital Fraud Victims

items.summary: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman blamed Google's AI search for a drop in referral traffic, warning total daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage from about 130 million in the fourth quarter. Shares fell 18% after earnings. Reddit plans to test logged-in-only access outside the US next quarter and will keep licensing its data with guardrails.
items.title: Reddit Mandates Logins as Google AI Search Cuts Traffic

items.summary: This week's VoxDevTalks episode featured several studies in development economics, reported by the outlet itself. Raúl Sánchez de la Sierra explains that around 250 armed groups tax villagers and provide security across eastern Congo. A city-wide experiment on progressive property tax in the Democratic Republic of Congo raised 56% more revenue than a proportional one with equal average liability, but only once enforcement targeted valuable properties.
items.title: This week in development economics at VoxDev: 30/10/2026

items.summary: China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Friday dismissed a New York Times report as unsubstantiated and a smear against China. The newspaper alleged that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le—a senior figure at Singapore-based Megaspeed—was gathering intelligence for Beijing with close ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and that President Donald Trump was briefed roughly a year ago but took no action. Guo called the claims nothing but a smear against China.
items.title: China Rejects NYT Report Linking Nvidia Ties to Beijing Intel

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is planning a pilot rollout from April 1, 2027, of polymer Rs10 and Rs20 banknotes while retaining their existing dimensions to minimise ATM modification costs. The approach would spare banks expenditure on replacing cash-dispensing cassettes, upgrading sensors and recalibrating machines. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra noted in August that polymer notes could last two to four times longer than conventional paper notes.
items.title: RBI Plans Polymer Rs10 and Rs20 Notes With Existing Dimensions From April 2027

items.summary: Oulu Police launched a criminal investigation into Tuike, Google's Finnish subsidiary, over suspected breaches of environmental law at planned data centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani. Forests were cleared before mandatory impact assessments finished; work is halted pending review. Detective Superintendent Kari Pakanen said the case concerns possible water act violations, with an update expected by December 2027.
items.title: Finnish police open probe into Google data centre forest clearings

items.summary: Apple announced its first touchscreen Macs, the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with a PRO OLED XDR display. Starting at $2,899 for the 14-inch version and configurable up to $14,549, they are available for preorder now and go on sale November 6. The touch input is not incidental but also not the main point; these machines target users seeking maximum technological sophistication in a portable Mac.
items.title: Apple Unveils First Touchscreen MacBook Pros With OLED Displays

items.summary: Microsoft is selling $25 billion in bonds as the AI buildout continues, Microsoft said. The senior unsecured notes mature between 2028 and 2066; proceeds may fund capital expenditures, buybacks or acquisitions, with net proceeds directed toward general corporate purposes. Two floating rate tranches of $1 billion each are due Nov. 3, 2028 and Nov. 3, 2029, alongside fixed rate notes from $2 billion of 4. 85% notes to $2 billion of 6. 35% notes. J. P. Morgan Securities, UBS Securities and Wells Fargo are among the joint book-running managers.
items.title: Microsoft Sells $25 Billion in Bonds for AI Buildout

items.summary: Sam Byford of Multicore reviews Apple’s eighth-generation iPad mini, noting the company calls it its biggest upgrade ever with an 8.5-inch OLED display and a new A20 Pro chip. However, he says Apple left out one feature that anyone with a recent iPhone is likely to notice as soon as they start scrolling: the screen stays locked at 60 Hz, without support for Apple’s 120 Hz ProMotion variable refresh rate technology. “I would have been all on board with an OLED iPad mini with ProMotion, but Apple lost my sale with this decision,” he wrote.
items.title: Apple Skips ProMotion on New iPad mini

items.summary: Intel shares fell more than 27% in premarket Friday trading after the chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion, heading toward its worst single-session performance ever, according to The Wall Street Journal. Nasdaq futures dropped more than 2%, and Amazon stock declined 6.5% Thursday following reported results.
items.title: Intel and Amazon losses trigger AI-driven tech selloff

items.summary: Samaya AI released Samaya Sterling, a LoRA post-trained model built on NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B total, 3B active parameters) for agentic financial research. On the FrontierFinance benchmark, it scores 58.9% at $0.61 per question versus Claude Fable 5.1’s 55.9% at $6.89 — an 11x cost reduction and a 3-point quality lead. Samaya states all results are self-reported on its own benchmark, with no training questions drawn from the test set. The gains come from co-training a small model with an adapted harness that merges tools, condenses context, and caps research length. Sterling scores lowest at 45.2% on the hardest third of queries.
items.title: Samaya AI Launches Low-Cost Finance Research Agent Model

items.summary: CGTN spoke with Professor Lin Jing of City University of Hong Kong and Professor Wen Yonggang of Nanyang Technological University about shared regional challenges. They said AI-powered weather systems, open-source public-health tools and embodied-intelligence robots could strengthen climate resilience, healthcare and social services across Asia-Pacific economies. Both experts noted the digital divide means uniform rollouts do not suit local conditions; instead they favour voluntary knowledge exchange, joint laboratories and capacity building.
items.title: APEC Economies Share Frontier Tech for Public Good

items.summary: Former Manipur chief minister N Biren Singh accused sections of the state BJP leadership of conspiring with the Congress to remove him from office, telling PTI that MLAs resent his elevation after switching parties. He questioned continued violence since his February 2025 resignation and urged the government to restore public trust ahead of early next year's assembly elections.
items.title: Ex-Manipur CM Biren Singh Blames BJP Leadership for Ouster Amid Continued Violence

items.summary: Fu Cong, China's permanent representative to the UN, called Thursday for emerging technologies such as AI and unmanned systems to better serve maritime security amid growing misuse risks. Speaking at a Security Council open debate on October 22, he urged greater international cooperation, equitable access for developing countries, and full adherence to the Law of the Sea.
items.title: China Envoy Urges Emerging Tech for Maritime Security

items.summary: Six people aboard a Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter died after it crashed near Chai village in Joshimath's Chamoli district, Uttarakhand. The aircraft departed Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1:14 pm before losing contact over the valley and being reported missing near Hathi Parvat. Police Superintendent Surjit Singh Panwar confirmed all six bodies were found. CEO Prateek Jain said local information prompted mobilising police, SDRF, Army and ITBP teams; the entire Trans Bharat fleet was grounded as a precaution amid heavy rain and snowfall. The cause remains unconfirmed. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami is monitoring the situation while rescue operations continue under adverse weather conditions expected to persist into November 1-2.
items.title: Uttarakhand Helicopter Crash Kills All Six on Board

items.summary: Shares of Laurus Labs climbed after it reported a sharp rise in second-quarter profit, driven by growth in its contract development and manufacturing organisation business and continued momentum from its Affordable Medicines division. The company posted net profit up 126% year on year to Rs 441 crore and EBITDA at Rs 762 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, while also declaring an interim dividend of Re 1 per share.
items.title: Laurus Labs Shares Rise on Strong Q2 Profit Jump

items.summary: As bird migration season begins, large flocks of birds are visible sweeping across the wetlands of the Shandong Yellow River Delta National Nature Reserve in east China's Shandong Province. Located along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, the reserve serves as a key stopover for migratory birds, providing habitat to rest, feed, molt, overwinter and breed.
items.title: Migratory Birds Sweep Across Shandong Wetlands in Migration Season

items.summary: Pingwang Park in Datong, Shanxi Province is glowing with golden autumn hues and drawing visitors to capture the season's beauty. Covering 280,000 square meters, the park blends classical Chinese garden design with waterfront landscapes, making it a beloved retreat for local residents.
items.title: Pingwang Park Glows With Golden Autumn Hues in Datong

items.summary: The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT) warned that European Union trade measures threaten a projected recovery in British vehicle production next year. An independent industry outlook forecasts annual output will decline this year before rising to 752,000 units in 2027 as new models enter production. The SMMT identified three major threats, including the EU's 'Made in EU' proposals and tougher rules of origin under the Trade Cooperation Agreement that could bring tariffs totaling 1. 4 billion pounds annually on two-way EV trade. Exports accounted for more than three-quarters of British vehicle production in September, with the EU receiving 57. 5% of those exports.
items.title: SMMT Warns EU Trade Measures Threaten UK Auto Recovery

items.summary: Nicola Shaw, chief executive of Yorkshire Water since 2022, announced she would step down on 1 January after the Environment Agency gave the firm one star out of four - its lowest possible rating. The company faced criticism over £1.9m in undisclosed payments and a £47m Ofwat fine for sewage leaks. MPs called for more than a leadership change to restore public trust.
items.title: Yorkshire Water CEO Resigns After Lowest Environmental Rating

items.summary: Blockchain firm Chainalysis reports that hackers behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft are using previously unseen laundering patterns to move funds ahead of freezes, while industry partners have begun freezing billions and Binance says it has reserved over $6.34B to cover losses; meanwhile Bitcoin fell below $80,000 amid speculation about North Korean involvement. (29 words)
items.title: Chainalysis flags novel laundering tactics in Binance heist as crypto markets wobble

items.summary: A study by the International Institute for Strategic Studies argues that Gulf states must rethink their trillion-dollar defence spending after a war with Iran. The report cites 4,670 Iranian drones and more than 1,400 ballistic missiles in weeks before an 8 April ceasefire, with nearly half aimed at the United Arab Emirates, and estimates energy-infrastructure damage as high as $58bn (£43bn). It says US bases offered little protection while exposing Gulf states to further attacks. Senator Chris Murphy added that rebuilding damaged bases may be pointless if they cannot be defended.
items.title: IISS Report Urges Gulf States to Reassess Trillion-Dollar US-Backed Defences

items.summary: A YouGov survey suggests voters view John Healey’s first budget as among the fairest for years, with nearly half (45%) calling it fair versus just 20% seeing it as not fair. The result contrasts sharply with last November’s budget, which 50% said would worsen household finances and only 3% better off. It outperforms Rachel Reeves’ previous budget on every measure assessed.
items.title: YouGov poll finds Healey budget seen as one of fairest in years

items.summary: Andreas Malm, a climate academic at Lund University, says he was denied entry to the UK after being told his presence was not conducive to the public good. He links it to a scheduled talk with Huda Ammori, founder of proscribed group Palestine Action, which he denies supporting or endorsing. The Home Office declined to comment on individual cases.
items.title: Swedish academic barred from UK over Palestine Action link

items.summary: Binance, described as the world's biggest crypto exchange, says it has been hit by a $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack believed to be the largest ever. The company said half of the stolen assets are frozen while much remains with hackers, and that it had begun recovering some funds. Two analytics firms attribute the attack to a North Korean hacking unit, though no one has claimed responsibility.
items.title: Binance Hit by Largest Crypto Hack in History

items.summary: Binance, described as the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, says it has suffered what is believed to be the largest crypto hack ever at $6.3bn (£4.7bn). Co-chief executive Richard Teng said Binance is working with authorities and will cover all losses from its emergency reserve plus company funds, while temporarily suspending deposits and withdrawals. Analytics firm TRM Labs noted similarities between this attack and a 2025 ByBit hack linked to North Korea's Lazarus Group, though the link remains unconfirmed. The exchange said around $3bn had been frozen so far and expected to resume withdrawals in 45 hours.
items.title: Binance faces record crypto hack amid North Korea suspicion

items.summary: BP reported its highest quarterly profit in nearly two decades, driven by elevated oil and gas prices from the war in Iran that widened refining margins. The company's underlying replacement cost profit rose to $8.46bn (£6.3bn), roughly four times the $2.2bn a year earlier, surpassing analysts' expectation of $7.3bn. BP chief executive Meg O'Neill called it a banner quarter for its refineries and said it captured market opportunities. The windfall drew criticism from climate campaigners Global Witness and Friends of the Earth over rising fuel costs. BP plans to clear Deepwater Horizon liabilities and may grow oil and gas production in an upcoming strategy update on 15 December.
items.title: BP Posts Record Profits Amid Middle East Conflict

items.summary: Scientists explore whether satellite imagery can anticipate catastrophic Himalayan slope failures. A synthesis report by ICIMOD scientists found that radar from Sentinel-1 and NISAR detected ground movement of up to 40 cm and 30 cm respectively before the August 26, 2026 Langtang Lirung collapse in Nepal. Yet these warning signs were not enough to predict when the slope would finally fail, as remote sensing involves huge data volumes. Experts call for better localised forecasts, rigorous monitoring, real-time systems and regional information-sharing across India, Nepal, Bhutan, China and Bangladesh through mechanisms like ICIMOD and WMO. Baral cautioned that detected movement does not necessarily mean collapse is imminent.
items.title: ICIMOD Scientists Probe Whether Satellites Can Forewarn Himalayan Slope Failures

items.summary: A cheetah named KNG22 died on October 27 at a veterinary facility in Jabalpur after being found injured with five recovered firearm pellets. The male was born to South African cheetah Nirva, brought under Project Cheetah. A government investigation team and Madhya Pradesh's Special Task Force were deputed to examine the incident. India's total cheetah population stands at 58, per a press note.
items.title: Cheetah cub dies from firearm pellet wounds in central India

items.summary: A guide explains specialist language in cryptocurrency news, opening with a report that the world's biggest crypto exchange said hackers had gained access to $6.3bn (£4.7bn) worth of digital assets and frozen about half while many remained stolen. The piece defines core concepts including Bitcoin as decentralised but volatile currency, blockchain technology, crypto exchanges and wallets (hot versus cold), Ethereum, ETFs such as spot Bitcoin products approved in January 2024 by the US, meme coins prone to rug pulls, stablecoins linked to assets like the dollar or pound sterling, and XRP with a fixed supply of 100 billion coins created at its 2012 launch. Prices are given exactly as written throughout, including Bitcoin topping $100,000 in December 2024 and rising to $120,000 in July 2025 before dipping below $65,000 in early February 2026.
items.title: Crypto Terms Explained From Bitcoin To Binance

items.summary: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting denied accusations of delaying defence spending decisions, responding to criticism from MPs on the Commons defence committee that key choices were postponed until next year's spending review. The row follows a government plan requiring foreign firms winning contracts over £50m to invest an equal value in UK factories and training by April 2027. Committee chair Tan Dhesi argued decisions had been deferred, warning of vulnerability in conflict; Streeting called the charge unfair and unfounded. Analysts question whether the UK can meet its target of spending 3% of GDP on defence by 2030,
items.title: Streeting Rejects Delay Charge Over Defence Spending

items.summary: NPR's Up First reports that Alaska's U.S. Senate race is facing claims of a spoiler candidate, after the New York Times revealed Democratic operatives were trying to recruit someone sharing incumbent GOP senator Dan Sullivan's name. Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation; election law experts found no applicable laws but said the conduct crosses ethical lines. Separately, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dismissed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia for overseeing Pentagon planning as U.S. and Israeli forces prepare for potential strikes on Iran.
items.title: Alaska Senate Race Faces Spoiler Claims; Hegseth Ousts Army General

items.summary: The Economic Times reports that TRAI has released draft guidelines establishing a framework for responsible AI adoption across India's telecommunications sector, which the Ministry of Communications describes as critical to national security and connectivity. The proposal builds on seven principles from earlier government guidelines and invites industry comments by November 27, 2026.
items.title: TRAI Releases Guidelines for Responsible AI in Telecom

items.summary: Texas announced it has taken control of nine islands in the water border between Mexico and the United States along its stretch from Laredo to McAllen, acting unilaterally on border-security grounds. Dawn Buckingham, the state land commissioner, authorized the National Guard to access them via a letter dated October 26. The Mexican government responded by asking that the 1970 Boundary Treaty be respected and insisting that only the International Boundary and Water Commission may determine the boundary. Rosario Sánchez of Binational Waters said such decisions are not a state matter, while scholar Gabriel Eckstein reframed the question as whether the islands belong to Texas or the federal government rather than Mexico. The decision remains on the IBWC’s agenda; this newspaper received no response from either its sections.
items.title: Mexico Calls for Treaty Respect After Texas Seizes Nine Rio Grande Islands

items.summary: Researchers reporting a discovery say they identified a new species of extinct gavial crocodile from fossils found in the Mokattam Formation near Giza, Egypt. The rocks that held them were used to carve the Great Sphinx about 4,500 years ago; both the sphinx and this fossil are missing their snout tips. CT scanning revealed anatomical differences—raised rims around the eye sockets absent in living gavials—that distinguish it from Tomistoma schlegelii, a species earlier proposed for these fossils. Led by Paul Burke of the Swedish Museum of Natural History with colleagues in Egypt and Germany, the team named it Herugavialis cairensis after Horus.
items.title: Egyptian fossil reveals new extinct crocodile species

items.summary: Researchers at Brazil's Pontifical Catholic University of Paraná (PUCPR) have proposed a decision-support framework to assess the recycling costs of photovoltaic systems, with an emphasis on emerging economies. The approach draws on a literature review and expert evaluation: searches in Scopus and Web of Science identified 5,784 records before yielding 23 studies reporting PV recycling costs, while 19 experts rated components on a five-point scale to retain 22 after screening. An adapted SWARA procedure assigned category weights, with operations and production highest at 21.71%. The team says the framework may be recalibrated for other regional settings.
items.title: Brazilian researchers propose PV panel recycling cost framework for emerging economies

items.summary:
Former India captain Sourav Ganguly has approached the Delhi High Court over the film Doosra, alleging that its makers used his identity, personal history and cricketing moments without consent. His dispute also involves an agreement with production house Luv Films dated 5 August, 2021, under which it holds rights to develop a biopic titled Dada covering his name, likeness, voice and life events. The filmmakers deny the film is about Ganguly, describing its fictional protagonist as inspired by him rather than based on him. They claim permission was obtained from BCCI, ECB and documentary producers for cricket footage. On 22 October the court refused to block the release; a hearing scheduled for November 2 may address scene edits or disclaimers before streaming platforms.
