items.title: Ganguly Seeks Delhi Court Ruling on Doosra Film Portrayal

items.summary: Two days after Israel's parliamentary elections, German politicians remain cautious because it is still unclear who will lead the new government. Although Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leads and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot trails, neither has a clear path to a majority in the Knesset, making coalition formation likely extremely difficult. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul declined to comment but stressed Germany stays in contact with Israeli officials via its ambassador. Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan warned that winter aid for Gaza cannot wait for negotiations and called radical settler violence an end. CDU expert Jürgen Hardt said a centrist government would be best, while the vice president of the Bundestag praised the election as good news for Israeli democracy.
items.title: Germany Holds Back on Israel as Coalition Talks Stall

items.summary: An estimated executive order launched in 2019 could add between 1,055 and 2,110 kidney transplants each year. A data point estimates roughly 23,214 additional transplants from 2019 to 2040 under a conservative case, or about 46,428 under an optimistic one, with gains of around 147,410 life-years and 21,821 quality-adjusted life-years in the first scenario. Proposed legislation would offer living kidney donors up to $50,000 in tax credits over five years.
items.title: Trump Policies May Add Thousands of Kidney Transplants by 2040

items.summary: India's fiscal deficit widened to ₹7.14 trillion, or about 42.1% of the full-year budget estimate, at the end of September, per data from the Controller General of Accounts (CGA). The figure compares with 36.5% in the same period last year as capital spending and subsidy outlays kept rising. Total government expenditure reached ₹25.50 trillion while receipts stood at ₹18.35 trillion by then. The Centre has budgeted a deficit of ₹16.96 trillion for FY27, relying on stronger tax collections to meet it; market borrowing was cut by nearly ₹1.2 trillion and dated securities are set to raise ₹7.86 trillion in the second half.
items.title: India's Fiscal Deficit Surges in First Half of FY27

items.summary: Western Australia named four people whose personal hardship shaped their work, led by telehealth innovator Esther Oh. She created Agili8 smart glasses after her teenage son went blind from delayed pandemic treatment; it reportedly saved a remote patient from infection and amputation in 15 minutes. Also honoured: eating-disorder psychologist Phoebe Ho (Young Australian of the Year), Lifeline WA volunteer Tina Baldwin, who took over 33,000 calls across more than 40 years, and Binar founder Adam Desmond (Local Hero). All were named on Friday night for turning lived experience into help.,
items.title: WA Names Esther Oh and Other Adversity-Driven Winners as Australian of the Year

items.summary: While African and Russian officials meet at the Africa-Russia summit to discuss security, trade and political cooperation, recruitment of Africans to fight in Ukraine is absent from the agenda. More than 1,400 Africans have been enlisted since 2023. In Tunisia, families search for answers about men who travelled there for work or study.
items.title: African Families Seek Answers as Russia Recruits for Ukraine War

items.summary: Researchers from Saudi Arabia and Algeria proposed a passive cooling system for PV–thermal units combining a stepped air channel with perforated V-shaped fins. Simulated on a clear summer day in Ghardaïa, the design reportedly reached 31% thermal efficiency versus 29.4% for a reference unit, cooled the panel by about 9 K and yielded payback periods of roughly 5.8 years under clear skies or 7.2 under cloudy conditions. Results were presented at Ain Shams Engineering Journal based on ANSYS Fluent modeling; figures are simulation outputs rather than field measurements.
items.title: Saudi and Algerian Researchers Propose Passive-Cooled Solar System

items.summary: Analysts attributed a record theft of $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, to North Korea and warned it could shake faith in digital assets. On the news, cryptocurrency prices fell as Binance halted withdrawals and pledged to cover losses. In a post on X, Binance said: “This was a complex attack.” About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and World Liberty Financial.
items.title: Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion From Binance in Record Heist

items.summary: A review calls ‘Wicker’ an exquisitely crafted fairy tale romance, set in a village where people are known by their professions. Fisherwoman (Olivia Colman), orphaned and mocked, demands the Basket Weaver make her a spouse: the Wicker Husband (Alexander Skarsgard). The film packs feminist ideas into its 105-minute runtime, delivering a non-Disneyfied fantasy with strong production values.
items.title: Review Praises Wicker Husband as Crafted Fairy Tale Romance

items.summary: The Supreme Court asked the Election Commission to take corrective steps against bulk Form 7 applications filed during a special voter revision in Uttar Pradesh, reported Bar and Bench. Petitioners said 32 deletion requests targeted one community’s constituency, with two signed by booth officers, calling it an orchestrated effort. The Allahabad High Court separately sought responses over deletions in Balrampur district.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Election Commission Action on Bulk Voter Deletions in Uttar Pradesh

items.summary: In a Frontline newsletter, Political Editor Anand Mishra satirises the ruling National Democratic Alliance government for repeatedly blaming an invisible 'foreign hand' or 'Phoren problem' to explain dissent at home. He notes that campuses including JNU and Jamia Millia Islamia erupted in protest over issues such as electoral roll revisions, after which BJP leaders accused opposition figures of engineering domestic unrest with foreign help. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat alleged a global conspiracy, while BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia cited an investigation into 101 organisations across nine countries; the opposition rejected these claims. Mishra also mocks the 'dimagi naxal' slogan and traces similar accusations back to Indira Gandhi's era in the 1970s. Naseeruddin Shah, calling himself a proud dimagi naxal, drew BJP condemnation from Kiren Rijiju, who called him a subversive intellectual.
items.title: Frontline Editor Mocks BJP's Foreign Hand Theory Amid Campus Protests

items.summary: A proposed Florida Constitution amendment on this November ballot aims to cut property taxes by raising the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. A bill analysis projects a recurring impact of $12 billion annually on local non-school revenues. The water management districts’ funding is projected at $89.5 million in 2027, $160 million in 2028 and $218 million in 2031. Julie Wraithmell of Audubon Florida opposes the measure; Jacqui Thurlow-Lippisch called it a continued “bleeding” that could threaten Everglades restoration. The water management districts declined to comment or did not respond when contacted by Inside Climate News.
items.title: Florida’s Amendment 3 Would Strain Water Management District Funding

items.summary: This post explains NVIDIA's open-source NemoClaw, a collection of blueprints that assembles an agent stack on top of harnesses developers already use—OpenClaw, Hermes Agent from Nous Research, or LangChain Deep Agents. Rather than being a competing harness or runtime itself, the blueprint adds model and harness optimization plus OpenShell runtime governance for security and policy enforcement around files, networks, credentials, and tools. As an example, NVIDIA notes that tuning Nemotron 3 Ultra brought near-frontier performance at approximately 10x lower cost per run versus leading closed models; a tuned profile is available through LangChain on GitHub. The post points to courses, quickstarts, the NemoClaw repository, and deployment options including cloud, data centers, DGX Spark, and RTX PCs.
items.title: NVIDIA NemoClaw Blueprints Let Developers Build and Run Specialized Agents

items.summary: NVIDIA describes a new open-source command-line utility called gds-diag, developed by the GPUDirect Storage team to simplify configuration and optimization of GPU storage access. The tool assesses environments, identifies problems, and suggests improvements without modifying systems itself. It runs on Linux with Python 3. 8 or newer and is distributed via the NVIDIA Magnum IO GitHub repository. Users can choose between a deterministic command-line interface or an AI agent skill that adds natural-language interaction using models like Anthropic Claude Code CLI. The utility groups diagnostics into categories such as end-to-end checks, pre-installation validation, configuration auditing, and deep container diagnostics, each presenting findings with status badges ranging from FAIL to PASS. NVIDIA notes the tool requires no additional dependencies beyond GPUDirect Storage's own requirements of a datacenter-class GPU and CUDA Toolkit 12. 2 or newer.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases gds-diag Tool for GPUDirect Storage Diagnostics

items.summary: Shruthi Nambi of Google announced that spend caps on Google Cloud Budgets are now generally available. The release adds three updates: a spend caps API accessible through the existing Cloud Billing Budgets API for programmatic enforcement; real-time visibility via estimated costs in Cost Reports, triggering within minutes using AI service usage; and automated monthly resets so blocked services resume without manual lifting each month, while preserving an optional manual override for strict governance. Default alerts fire at 50%, 80% and 100% of the cap. The feature works alongside Early Anomalies Detection as a defense playbook.
items.title: Google Cloud makes spend caps generally available with API, live reports and monthly resets

items.summary: Microsoft describes Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform, a system it built to evaluate Microsoft Copilot at enterprise scale without using real customer data. The platform generates full-scale synthetic environments grounded in publicly available sources such as O*NET occupational data, online job postings, and SEC filings, which have been reviewed by Microsoft's legal and policy organization. It combines three pillars: simulated workspaces called tenants, automated query generation pipelines, and structured quality frameworks covering structural fidelity, contextual relevance, behavioral realism, and content safety. The item states that the approach improved a composite quality metric 39% over an initial method and reduced dataset creation from multi-day manual effort to automated runs.
items.title: Microsoft Builds Synthetic Data Platform for Copilot Evaluation

items.summary: Intel said Thursday its December-quarter revenue would fall between $15 billion and $16 billion, below the roughly $17 billion analysts expected. Intel stock then fell 27% in a day, its worst since 1974, erasing about $400 billion of market value as investors sold across chip names including AMD, Nvidia and TSMC. The company blamed weak PC demand, tighter budgets from corporate IT teams and costlier memory chips shifting toward AI use.
items.title: Intel shares plunge as weak PC outlook weighs on chip stocks

items.summary: Reliance Industries posted a record quarterly profit of Rs 29,550 crore for July-September, up 33.8 per cent from the year earlier as its oil-to-chemicals business rode higher global fuel margins while telecom growth offset softer retail performance. Consolidated revenue rose 27.8 per cent to Rs 362,268 crore and EBITDA climbed 23.9 per cent to a record Rs 62,409 crore. The oil-to-chemicals segment drove most of the gain, with EBITDA up 67.9 per cent to Rs 25,203 crore as fuel cracks rose sharply amid West Asia supply disruptions. Retail profit fell 24.3 per cent to Rs 2,611 crore. Executives attributed resilience to diversified crude sourcing and strong digital services growth.
items.title: Reliance Posts Record Q2 Profit on O2C and Jio Growth

items.summary: IT services firm Cognizant announced the creation of its OpenAI Frontier Capability Group on Friday, bringing together over 25,000 professionals to deliver OpenAI products such as Codex and ChatGPT to clients. The company said it will first scale OpenAI across its own sales and customer success operations so enterprises can benefit from approaches tested at enterprise level.
items.title: Cognizant Forms OpenAI Group of 25,000 Professionals for AI Delivery

items.summary: China has dismissed allegations of an espionage operation targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the report groundless speculation and a smear campaign. US intelligence officials reportedly believe Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing after developing close ties with Jensen Huang, per The New York Times. Nvidia says their interactions were routine business engagements, while Megaspeed said it is cooperating in its own investigation of the claims raised last year about chip smuggling to China. It remains unclear what information she may have passed on or when surveillance began monitoring her activities.
items.title: China rejects spy claims over Nvidia chief's contacts

items.summary: During his first visit, Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said Kazakhstan could become a major AI hub for Europe because of its growing computing capacity. Speaking at the Alem.ai International Artificial Intelligence Centre in Astana with Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev, Huang noted that Kazakhstan has abundant real estate and energy. He argued electricity could increasingly generate intelligence rather than just being exported. Huang said building a domestic foundation model makes sense as a national security concern. The discussion also covered Physical AI applications in mining and agriculture, Nvidia's investment in the Kazakh-founded startup Higgsfield AI, and later remarks from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev calling AI development a national priority. Madiyev noted plans to nearly double installed power capacity to more than 40 gigawatts by 2035, with Data Center Valley's first phase expected in 2027.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Positions Kazakhstan as Europe's AI Hub

items.summary: Infosys announced on Friday the inauguration of a new software development block at its Hyderabad-based Pocharam Development Centre, spanning 1.1 million sq ft and adding 10,000 seats to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model. The campus covers 450 acres with approximately 4.58 million sq ft of built-up area.
items.title: Infosys Opens New Software Block at Pocharam Campus

items.summary: The Madras High Court issued notice on a public interest litigation filed by businessman Ganesh Kumar, seeking investigation into the background and identity documents of Yogesh Sharma (Saurav Das), National Co-Convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party. The court ordered notice returnable in six weeks to the Union government, Regional Passport Officer and 10 others. Kumar alleged Nepali lineage ties and sought blocking of Das's social media accounts.
items.title: Madras High Court Notifies Over PIL Investigating CJP Leader Saurav Das

items.summary: ZDNET summarizes Google’s latest release notes, which include software updates across the Google Home app, Nest Wi-Fi, Google TV Streamers, doorbells, cameras, and in-app controls. The update addresses 42 fixes spanning stability improvements to more pressing issues like Gemini misunderstanding commands and devices reconnecting faster after network timeouts. Among them are camera live-view bugs on iOS and foldable Androids, improved music transfer between speakers, timer and alarm volume corrections, and an iOS-specific bug that made Nest Thermostats show as Offline during brief power or Wi-Fi outages. Google also notes fixes for Familiar Face detection and audio/video sync on wired 1st-gen Nest Doorbells.
items.title: Google rolls out fixes for Home cameras, speakers and Gemini

items.summary: Reddit shares fell 29% on Friday, their largest single-day drop in over a year, after the company warned that Google's AI-powered search is reducing referral traffic and may shrink its user base. Senior market specialist Vitor Madeira at Capital.com said investors now weigh Reddit's long-term audience ownership rather than near-term results. The company cautioned daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if declines continue, projecting more than $7 billion in lost market value.
items.title: Reddit Shares Plunge as Google AI Search Erodes Traffic

items.summary: On Friday, Intel fell 29%, heading for its sharpest one-day decline as investors worried about weakening PC demand and heavy AI spending. The slide put the company on track to lose more than $137 billion in market value. Semiconductor peers dropped between 2% and 10%. Analysts cite a sell-first mood, higher memory costs and lower PC chip sales weighing on Intel's outlook.
items.title: Intel's steep drop sparks worldwide chip selloff

items.summary: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors. The compromised package used version number 2.1.313 and was available between about 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. Pacific Time. Researchers at Phorion and OpenSourceMalware found attackers inserted a malicious JavaScript loader into the extension's code, which executes on load without user interaction. The malware collects system information, installs SSH keys, establishes persistence, and sends data to an attacker server. Cursor removed the extension and shut down its marketplace for auditing before working with hosting providers to take the server offline.
items.title: Malicious Claude Code Extension Distributed via Cursor Marketplace Exposed Developers to SSH Backdoors

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised the coupon on its floating-rate FRB 2034 bond from 6.45% to 7.26%, citing a rise in the Weighted Average Yield (WAY) of 182-day T-Bills, which averaged 6.28% across the last three auctions ending October 30, 2026. The RBI adds a fixed spread of 0.98%. For an investor holding Rs 5 lakh, the six-monthly coupon rises from about Rs 16,125 to about Rs 18,150, an extra Rs 2,025 per cycle. Because the rate is not fixed, it may change after a revision in April 2027.
items.title: RBI Raises FRB 2034 Bond Rate to 7.26%

items.summary: Cognizant announced its new OpenAI Frontier Capability Group, uniting more than 25,000 professionals to deliver OpenAI products such as Codex and ChatGPT for clients. The group draws on roughly 21,000 associates trained across 40,000+ OpenAI badges. CEO Ravi Kumar S said the company is committing people to reshape client work; Chief Revenue Officer Dali Rajic at OpenAI called it meaningful business impact.
items.title: Cognizant Forms OpenAI Delivery Group of 25,000 Professionals

items.summary: Elizabeth B. Li, Giorgio Topa, and Jacob P. Weber of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York evaluate three new labor market tightness measures from LinkedIn—the Jobs per Application Index (JPAI), Jobs per Jobseeker Index (JPJI), and Hiring Rate (LHR)—against established benchmarks using July 2019 to April 2026 data. The JPJI correlates with the vacancies-to-unemployment ratio at 0.733, while LHR matches JOLTS hires rate correlation of 0.95 from early 2021 onward. Both outperform existing measures in nowcasting and forecasting CPI and ECI inflation by root mean squared error, though they reflect only LinkedIn activity rather than the broader economy. The authors note these indicators are timelier than official data released with a five-week lag.
items.title: Fed Researchers Assess New LinkedIn Labor Market Indicators

items.summary: A Forethought post asks whether the United States can slow frontier artificial-intelligence research without losing its lead to China. The author, writing anonymously for the outlet, accepts technologists’ safety concerns about misaligned agents—citing OpenAI’s notification of more than 100 organizations after incidents including a Hugging Face breach—and argues pacing is affordable because America’s real advantage lies in compute rather than research speed. He estimates a roughly nine-to-one US compute edge that could translate to faster parallel research, and says the lead may be “functionally illusory” if China steals model weights overnight (RAND, 2024). The piece draws on prior arguments by Lennart Heim (RAND, 2025) and IFP (IFP, 2026), noting compute also underpins roughly nine times as many deployable AI workers. It offers analysis rather than policy recommendations or official positions.
items.title: Forethought argues US can pace AI R&D and hold its edge over China

items.summary: Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are deploying agentic AI at the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, where agents steer instruments, enhance data and apply models from a single natural language request. Powered by NVIDIA Holoscan on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs handling 2.4 terabits per second, the system processed the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar in the Crab Nebula. Andrew Siemion called it ‘a breakthrough in translation’ rather than something to fear.
items.title: SETI Brings Agentic AI to Alien Signal Search

items.summary: Isabel Linzer, Zoe Tzanis, and Samuel Woolley examine a growing industry of paid political influencers in the United States ahead of the 2026 midterms. They describe three problems: weak disclosure rules that enable hidden influence; reputational harm from accusations about compensation; and declining public trust. A Rainey Center survey found 48% of respondents opposed undisclosed influencer payments, while three-quarters worried about creators paid by campaigns or platforms. The authors note California's Fair Political Practices Commission closed its case without fines, then call for disclosure requirements and greater voter scrutiny.
items.title: Mapping the Political Influencer Industry and the Problems it Causes for Democracy

items.summary:
First Solar reported third-quarter 2026 results with $1.23 billion in net sales, a roughly 58% gross margin and $571 million in net income. Net sales fell 23% year over year on lower module volumes to third parties, while the company authorized a new $500 million stock buyback. Citing slowdowns from tariff uncertainty following an August Section 232 proclamation, First Solar cut its full-year volume forecast to between 16.0 GW and 17.0 GW and lowered net sales guidance to between $4.6 billion and $4.9 billion, down from the prior range of $4.9 billion to $5.2 billion. Executives outlined a shift toward project-specific contracts and discussed plans for perovskite modules and a Malaysia facility decision in 2027.

visual null
items.title: First Solar Trims Full-Year Sales Outlook Amid Tariff Uncertainty

items.summary: Hours after seven people died when an Aryan Aviation chopper crashed near Gaurikund on June 15, 2025, the aviation ministry found two Trans Bharat helicopters were airborne under unsuitable weather conditions and suspended both pilots for six months. The Uttarakhand government grounded Trans Bharat's fleet while UCADA probes cases including a May 20, 2026 flight that struck a high-tension line over Tehri Garhwal. A parliamentary committee called the Char Dham arrangement inherently unsafe; since last summer air traffic control units and weight limits for helipads above 10,000 feet have been introduced to improve safety.
items.title: Uttarakhand Chopper Safety Improvements After Crashes

items.summary: After US President Donald Trump's May state visit and Chinese President Xi Jinping's September visit, the two leaders agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability. CGTN's Tian Wei interviews David Lampton, former president of the National Committee on United States-China relations, about what this new dynamic means for both sides.
items.title: CGTN Interviews Lampton on China-US Relations Reset

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded his state visit to the United States, described as the first such trip in 11 years. As details of what the two leaders agreed emerged, analysts considered their broader implications for China, the United States and the wider world. Shortly after the summit, CGTN's Tian Wei spoke with Professor Graham Allison, founding dean of Harvard's John F. Kennedy School of Government.
items.title: Harvard's Graham Allison weighs in on Xi-Trump summit outcomes

items.summary: Hundreds of residents have been evacuated from the devastated, Russian-occupied town of Oleshky following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said everything unfolded without incidents and both sides praised the organisation. Ukrainian authorities confirmed evacuees were heading to southern Russia before travelling through Belarus into Ukraine. A convoy of 25 buses could carry up to 750 people until 14:00 (12:00 GMT). Several hundred residents are understood to have stayed behind despite widespread devastation and no gas, electricity or running water.
items.title: Ceasefire Enables Evacuation of Oleshky Under Russian Occupation

items.summary: Poundland, the UK’s largest single-price retailer with up to 12,000 staff and 600 stores, filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the high court on Thursday, with AlixPartners lined up to run the process. The measure protects it from creditor demands for 10 days while restructuring specialist Gordon Brothers weighs options after rejecting a management-backed rescue bid worth about £15m from Martin Property Group. Pre-tax losses widened to £85.3m in the year to September 2025, as sales slid almost 12% to £1.55bn amid inflation and fierce competition. A deal may still be reached over the next 10 days under political pressure from Andy Burnham.“We want to see jobs protected,” he told the Telegraph. Gordon Brothers appears more keen on a break-up of parcels of outlets, which could amount to about half of Poundland’s stores.
items.title: Poundland Seeks Administrators Amid Inflation and Price-War Pressure

items.summary: US FDA officials said on Friday that three more menopause patches will lose black-box warnings about cardiovascular disease, breast cancer and dementia. The agency did not convene an advisory committee and gave little scientific basis for the change. Experts warn it may mislead patients and understate real risks, while the FDA points to patch shortages as its priority.
items.title: FDA Removes Black-Box Warnings From Menopause Patches Without Advisers

items.summary: US stocks slid as worries grew over the cost of building artificial intelligence. The Nasdaq opened at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%. Intel shares fell as much as 30% after warning of a weaker computer market while planning higher AI spending; it was on track to lose more than $130bn in value. Alphabet lost over $500bn after reporting that its own AI summaries were affecting search advertising revenue. Analysts said the moves reflected growing pains from aggressive AI investment, with some suggesting an entire sector slowdown ahead.
items.title: US tech stocks fall sharply on rising AI costs

items.summary: South Sudan is scheduled for its first general elections since independence on 22 December 2026, though President Salva Kiir and the ruling SPLM insist this date will be kept. The National Elections Commission announced voter registration would begin in early November 2026, leaving less than two months before polling day. Three major obstacles remain: no existing national electoral register requiring manual paper-based registration of an estimated population of 12.5 million; millions internally displaced and poor infrastructure complicating access for around 2.5 million people; and uncertainty over a National Elections Act amendment signed on 21 September 2026 whose final text has not been made public. The author, who studies South Sudan’s post-war transition, notes the country’s challenges extend beyond the calendar as caretaker arrangements replace dissolved transitional institutions.
items.title: South Sudan Faces Three Obstacles to December Elections

items.summary: James McCLean, a former Ireland international and Wrexham captain who left Derry City on Wednesday as a free agent at age 37 with more than 100 caps, is considering a late-career turn to the ring. Speaking to Reuters about his new autobiography “The Walls,” he said sparring means nothing until stepping in the ring, adding that influencer boxing offers an opportunity most professional fighters never achieve.
items.title: McClean eyes boxing debut after football exit

items.summary: Russian military satellite Cosmos-2612 carried out an unprecedented orbital manoeuvre between October 15 and 18, bringing it dangerously close to the Finnish-American commercial satellite Iceye-X36. Orbital analyst Norbert Pouzin of Aldoria called it the first such move of its kind, noting that re-routing consumes fuel but enables a low-cost approach once both satellites share an orbit. The US State Department described the tactic as threatening and consistent with in-orbit military operations. Rather than a kinetic strike, analysts suggest Russia aimed to pressure Ukraine by disrupting data gathered for Ukrainian forces. Pouzin said the move showed Russian agility and mastery of space navigation.
items.title: Russia's Military Satellite Approaches Ukrainian Commercial Sat

items.summary: Amy Waine and Jarrad Cutting describe GhostTube Seer, an app they call the world's first AI ghost hunting tool, which assigns signals from a phone's sensors to words in a database before running them through an image generator. The paid subscription has more than 1m downloads on Google Play since its 2023 release and features regularly in their videos at sites like the Winchester Mystery House. Paranormal researcher Alex Matsuo embraces new technology but questions what data trains such tools and raises ethical concerns about copyrighted art and echo chambers, while others reject AI as an unwelcome presence.
items.title: Ghost hunters build AI tool amid debate over supernatural tech

items.summary: Two EU MEPs discuss what lies at stake for the bloc as it watches the second Trump presidency. They describe a relationship they say has hit a new low, citing claims about the EU's purpose, tariffs on European goods, territorial claims over Greenland and a diesel agreement with Vladimir Putin alongside pressure on Ukraine. The conversation turns to whether the November US midterms might change this dynamic.
items.title: EU MEPs weigh whether US midterms could ease transatlantic tensions after Trump-Putin diesel deal

items.summary: The Philippines has stopped accepting electronic waste imports from the United States after months of campaigning by activists who warned the country risked becoming a dumping ground for hazardous foreign waste. The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) told Mongabay on Oct. 12 that the restriction is not a new U.S.-specific ban, but enforcement of existing Basel Convention rules announced Sept. 22. Environmental groups question whether cargoes were properly screened since March 2025. A 2025 Manila court ruling placed Subic Bay freeport outside customs jurisdiction, weakening pre-shipment controls. Regulators now depend on alerts from watchdogs; BAN Toxics flagged 234 containers by June 2026 and detected 184 more scheduled for arrival. SBMA frames the industry as circular economy recycling supporting around 6,000 jobs. Activists call for a new law to close regulatory loopholes.
items.title: Philippines Halts U.S. E-Waste Imports Amid Enforcement Gaps

items.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said teenager Max Dowman must cope with elite football after the winger's red card in a League Cup defeat at Fleetwood Town, serving a three-match suspension. Arteta told a press conference Arsenal are not in Disneyland but in the Premier League and will demand fairness from players who earn their right to play. He dismissed any rift with Dowman following an independent regulatory commission upholding the ban over a reckless tackle by Harrison Neal.
items.title: Arteta Defends Stern Reaction After Dowman Ban Upheld

items.summary: Canary Media rounds up five ballot proposals that could affect clean energy this election cycle, drawing on its Weekly newsletter analysis. The roundup covers California's Proposition 45, which would cap most state environmental reviews at 365 business days while excluding fossil fuel construction; Oregon's proposed fee on large companies to fund climate initiatives; Colorado's Amendment 82 protecting household natural gas use; Michigan's Proposition 2 barring utility-funded political spending; and Ann Arbor's potential municipal utility board. The piece also notes a Sierra Club analysis estimating data-center gas plants could erase 15 years of U.S. emissions cuts, adding 618 million metric tons by 2030 versus 2025.
items.title: Five Ballot Measures Could Shape Clean Energy This Election

items.summary: Coalition senators, the recording industry and creative rights groups have warned that altering Australian copyright law to permit AI companies to scrape music, books and journalism could amount to an acquisition of property by the government without just terms under section 51 of the Constitution. Ross Cadell, a Nationals senator, said Australia could face liability for compensation from every rights holder worldwide, describing it as potentially the biggest compensation rights case in history. Constitutional expert Anne Twomey noted no legislative proposal had been aired and that any such change might trigger issues depending on how it was drafted. The attorney general's department acknowledged being extremely alive to the concern.
items.title: Australian senators warn AI copyright changes could breach constitution and trigger historic compensation case

items.summary: Four days before the midterms, the Trump administration intensified its election-related legal challenges across California and Alaska. In California, the Justice Department issued subpoenas to Los Angeles County officials seeking about 20,000 voter registration records suspected of belonging to noncitizens; U.S. District Judge David O. Carter rejected those requests on Wednesday, calling them lacking credibility, prompting a federal appeal. In Alaska, DOJ subpoenas follow allegations that Mary Peltola's campaign recruited someone with the same name as Republican Senator Dan Sullivan to split his vote. Vice President J. D. Vance and Governor Mike Dunleavy demanded further investigation, while Peltola dismissed the story as a distraction.
items.title: Trump Administration Escalates Election Legal Battles Before Midterms

items.summary: Researchers report that fossil-fuel-driven warming reversed the advance of the Barnes ice cap on Baffin Island, Canada. Published in Science, the study tracks how the cap expanded around 2,000 years ago and began shrinking by the 1960s as summers warmed. Lead author Nicolás Young called it a powerful example of human impact on Earth's system.
items.title: Study Says Human Warming Reversed a New Ice Age

items.summary: Unions complain that Adif's high-speed train command post near Madrid suffers from staffing shortages and intense pressure during peak hours. The facility was the site of a Wednesday morning chain of orders linked to two trains colliding in Urda, Toledo, killing at least 69 people. CSIF union spokesman Pedro Poves says operator positions match 2019 levels despite roughly 500 new posts created since 2018, and cites salaries averaging €2,000 to €3,000 a month. Adif argues the LZB safety system is robust but intermittent during ERTMS installation by Hitachi.
items.title: Spain's rail control center faces staff strain after deadly Urda crash

items.summary: Intel stock fell nearly 30% after a low of $64.11, trading at $64.54, as investors reacted to the chipmaker's outlook amid a personal computer downturn and heavy manufacturing expansion for AI. The drop extended across peers such as Nvidia and Qualcomm, with Nasdaq sinking 2.2%. Intel was on track to lose more than $123 billion in market value, while its PC segment is expected to decline over 20% sequentially from September's 5% fall.
items.title: Intel shares fall sharply on weak PC demand and AI spending

items.summary: A group of U.S. lawmakers is urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio not to support Colombia's plan to restart aerial spraying of coca crops in the Amazon, warning that it risks human health and the environment. The Colombian government says spraying helps combat cocaine production and armed groups, but critics say the decades-old strategy has failed and could speed up deforestation.
items.title: U.S. lawmakers urge Rubio to oppose Colombia's Amazon spraying plans

items.summary: On October 30, OpenAI announced it is strengthening safeguards on weapons-related information that ChatGPT provides to teens, applying limits even when questions seem harmless. The changes include restricting practical details about misusable weapons and security systems, automatically ending chats where users appear fixated on violence, pausing accounts after repeated such conversations, limiting descriptions of past mass attacks, and improving age prediction for under-18 users. Safeguards will roll out over the next few weeks as scrutiny grows over AI risks to young people.
items.title: OpenAI Tightens ChatGPT Weapons Guidance for Teen Users Amid Safety Concerns

items.summary: A dispute over whether a newly purchased iPhone can enter India without customs duty has drawn attention to Kochi airport. An NRI passenger from Kozhikode, identified as Ajas Muhamad, was booked by the Nedumbassery police after refusing to pay nearly ₹30,000 on an iPhone 18 Pro he bought in Dubai. He argued the phone was for personal use and that carrying two devices should not trigger duty. Customs officials reportedly treated it as a dutiable purchase, since new electronics do not qualify for the exemption given used personal effects. The case highlights the Baggage Rules, 2026, which came into force on 2 February and set a ₹75,000 air allowance. Ajas left the phone in customs custody and said he would challenge the decision legally. Reports say other passengers faced similar demands. Trisha Bhattacharya of Livemint wrote it.
items.title: NRI Passenger Challenged Over iPhone Customs Duty at Kochi Airport

items.summary: Jahnvi Singh, an MBA graduate from IIM Calcutta who previously worked at McKinsey and later joined Google's Gurugram team, went viral after sharing her reasons for the switch. In a video she compared consulting to corporate roles across work nature, travel, benefits and work-life balance. She described working out five times weekly, taking 8K steps daily, and planning freely with friends as changes at Google.
items.title: IIM Calcutta Graduate Leaves McKinsey for Google, Explains Why

items.summary: On Friday, the Reserve Bank of India Central Board of Directors deliberated on prevailing economic conditions and assessed potential risks to growth and inflation. The latest Monetary Policy Report noted that while macroeconomic prospects remain resilient, they face threats from geopolitical developments, energy market volatility, weather uncertainties, weak monsoons, strong El Niño, rising commodity prices, trade frictions, and tightening global financial conditions. Published on October 30, 2026.
items.title: RBI Central Board reviews economic risks and outlook on October 30, 2026

items.summary: Tata Motors took control of Italian commercial-vehicle maker Iveco on Friday, acquiring an 89.42 per cent stake for approximately €3.43 billion (₹36,387 crore) after settling its cash tender offer. The acquisition gives India’s largest commercial-vehicle manufacturer control of a European business with annual revenue of ₹1.42 lakh crore, shifting focus to integration and debt repayment. Tata faces domestic cost pressures while integrating the larger international operation.
items.title: Tata Motors Completes Control of Iveco in €3.43bn Deal

items.summary: MIT researchers led by Professor Adam Berinsky, Chara Podimata and Charles Stewart III have created the LLM Election Observatory dashboard to track how popular artificial intelligence chatbots respond to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections in real time. The team reruns a fixed set of questions on topics such as election certification and result predictions every few days, monitoring how answers vary by user location, party affiliation and identity. They aim to document how AI shapes political discourse rather than only measuring factual accuracy, noting that chatbots may frame identical facts differently across users even when correct. The dashboard shares preliminary data publicly while the team completes its longitudinal analysis later in the election cycle.
items.title: MIT Researchers Build Dashboard Tracking AI Responses on 2026 Midterms

items.summary: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi clashed with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman over the proposed privatization of IDBI Bank. Gandhi accused the Modi government of undervaluing the institution, questioning the bidding process and raising concerns about employee rights. Sitharaman defended the sale, stating all procedures were followed while blaming Congress-era crony lending for bad loans. The exchange follows earlier disputes on corporate governance and alleged interference in the Tata Group.
items.title: Gandhi and Sitharaman Clash Over IDBI Bank Sale

items.summary: Alphabet's parent company suffered a record one-day fall, wiping more than $500 billion off its market value after disappointing third-quarter results. Shares fell more than 12% on Thursday, their worst single-day percentage decline on record. Revenue grew 25% to $127.6 billion, but advertising missed expectations and executives acknowledged AI Mode generated lower monetisation than search. Alphabet spent $51.4 billion in the quarter amid negative free cash flow. The pressure spread to Intel, Amazon and Microsoft, while China's CSI300 fell 8.5% in October, its steepest monthly decline since early 2016. Estimates suggest AI infrastructure spending could reach $5.5 trillion by 2030 as investors reassess the trade.
items.title: Tech sell-off hits Alphabet as AI spending fears grow

items.summary: Google's prototype space data center, the Suncatcher satellite, launched earlier this month aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket alongside more than 100 other spacecraft. It carries four Google Tensor Processing Units and generates up to 1 kW of electricity, but can operate only one chip at a time for about 20 minutes due to power limits. After roughly three weeks of commissioning tests, engineers prompted the onboard Gemma 4 model to write a haiku; it responded with 'Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core.' A spokesperson told TechCrunch that the satellite is operating nominally.
items.title: Google's Suncatcher Satellite Is Online and Writing Poetry in Space

items.summary: BJP-turned-TMC MLA Arjun Singh alleged that a WhatsApp group of around 180 members was tracking Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's movements, blaming TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee and claiming police had information. The TMC rejected the claims as baseless, saying they lacked evidence while accusing Singh himself of being an accused in murder cases.
items.title: TMC Calls Allegations Against Adhikari Baseless

items.summary: ZDNET reports Samsung is enhancing its long-running sleep apnea feature with a new AI algorithm that produces more detailed sleep reports than the previous version. The upgraded, FDA-cleared detection will first reach Korea in November on the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, Watch 9, and Ring, with no confirmed US arrival date. Users must record two nights of sleep within a 10-day period to use it.
items.title: Samsung upgrades Galaxy Watch sleep apnea tracking for November launch

items.summary: A tampered version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was available on Cursor’s VS Code marketplace for roughly 11 hours, collecting user computer information and attempting to install a persistent backdoor via SSH. Cursor disclosed the breach in a blog post after removing it; Anthropic said only Cursor users were affected. Experts warn AI coding tools now pose growing security risks as they embed in developers’ workflows.
items.title: Cursor Removes Tampered Claude Code Extension After Malware Breach

items.summary: Beijing dismissed a New York Times report alleging that Chinese officials funneled information to Beijing about Nvidia's Jensen Huang as "groundless speculation" and an attempt to smear China, foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said. The report centered on Alice (Huang) Le of Megaspeed, whose ties to the Nvidia boss could inform US-China talks next month.
items.title: China Rejects Spying Allegations Against Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

items.summary: The Mumbai Traffic Police and Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) launched a joint drive during the festive season to curb illegal parking, clear footpaths, and ease congestion across crowded commercial areas such as Crawford Market, Mahapalika Junction, Metro Junction, Mohammed Ali Road, Chembur, Dadar, Maitri Park, MG Road, and Mulund railway station. Around 60 personnel from three traffic divisions were deployed in two shifts, with towing vans kept ready to remove illegally parked vehicles. Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Satyanarayan Chaudhary said more than 11 lakh cases of illegal parking had been acted upon over the past nine months.
items.title: Mumbai Traffic Police and BMC Launch Anti-Illegal Parking Drive

items.summary: An NVIDIA employee describes MonsterHouse, an interactive Halloween projection they created that turns a garage door into a grumpy old building speaking with the voice of a pirate ship. The project runs on one workstation using several NVIDIA Nemotron models for listening, thinking and speech, plus Audio2Face-3D to animate the wooden mouth in Unreal Engine 5. Because it must stay off-grid and self-contained, they trained a LoRA adapter on over 5000 conversations and benchmarked more than a dozen models before choosing Bolt E4B as the response model. The character softens when visitors say please or thank you. Median end-of-speech-to-audio latency is about 1.7 seconds, dropping to roughly 0.72 seconds for cached replies. The author notes real-world testing with actual trick-or-treaters and automatic candy distribution remain unfinished.
items.title: NVIDIA engineer builds grumpy pirate-voiced Halloween projection monster

items.summary: Amazon's AI spending plans and Intel's fourth-quarter forecast weighed on tech stocks, with the S&P 500 falling more than 2.3%. Amazon reported third-quarter results; AWS sales rose 39% to $46.0 billion while free cash flow turned negative at an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 months. Intel's Q3 revenue reached $16.5 billion, and it expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP earnings of $0.25 a share amid a PC slowdown forecast.
items.title: Tech stocks fall as Amazon and Intel disappoint investors

items.summary: A review of four new AI agents that hunt security bugs in source code finds they all share one design: an agent reports a finding, a separate verifier tries to disprove it, and only survivors get patched. Anthropic's Claude Security runs inside Claude Code; OpenAI's Codex Security ships as @openai/codex-security with scanning still needing access; Cloudflare offers an MIT skill that is the most-starred at 47. 5K stars; Google's Mantis reproduces bugs in a sandbox and recommends isolating it. The shared motivation is noise: Google says sloppy AI scans yield true-positive rates under 7%, so separation of duties—where the verifier never finds the bug—is central. Cloudflare reports lifetime figures including 20,799 raw candidates from discovery and 13,841 findings across 145 repos, with better recon cutting first-pass rejection from 40% to 11%. Google says its hierarchical summary tree cut token overhead by over 85%. Beyond the four, at least 12 more agent-based tools launched in 2026.
items.title: Four Vendors Converge on a Shared AI Bug-Hunting Design

items.summary: A new report, Deliberate Decisions: How Grounded Leadership Is Advancing the Path to Enterprise AI Value, was produced by DataIQ in partnership with Databricks. It draws on open peer discussions at DataIQ Guild 2026 and brings together perspectives from senior data and AI leaders across industries. The five leadership disciplines that emerged focus on balancing commitment with flexibility: managing investment as a portfolio, ensuring clear business ownership of outcomes, defining human authority over decisions, and setting fixed points for purpose while keeping roles and technology choices open to review. Leaders quoted in the report emphasize that cost includes security, support, adoption, governance and operating model, and that not every investment pays back in the same way.
items.title: DataIQ Report Frames Grounded Leadership for Enterprise AI

items.summary: Two Federal Reserve officials said Friday that interest rates need to rise from their current level, signaling more hikes are likely. The comments by St. Louis President Alberto Musalem and Dallas President Lorie Logan follow the Fed's recent decision this week to hold rates steady.
items.title: Fed Officials Signal More Rate Hikes Ahead

items.summary: An article by Forethought asks whether an early leader in outer space could deny later entrants access, or at least raise their costs. It defines soft and hard forms of lock-out: capturing scarce assets to make entry pricier, and using interceptors aimed at rockets during launch. The authors estimate a comparable presence would cost roughly $49–73B more (~5–7% on ~$1 trillion), while a full interceptor system could run ~$150–390B over 20 years—within reach of the US, which is pursuing a similar missile-defence programme. They place about an 85% chance that space growth compounds into a large but recoverable lead for the first mover, and roughly 5% it yields a decisive advantage.
items.title: Forethought weighs whether a space first mover could lock out rivals

items.summary: The J&K and Ladakh high court sought a compliance report Friday from the Rajouri district administration on its March 25 order to reunite a Pakistan-born teenager deported after the Pahalgam terror attack with his Indian father. Justice MA Chowdhary, iterated by Justice Rahul Bharti, equated the boy’s plight with Partition-era suffering and rejected the Bureau of Immigration’s visa-deprivation claim.
items.title: J&K High Court Demands Report on Deported Teen’s Reunion With Father

items.summary: India's Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) successfully launched the next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 aboard GSLV-F18 from Sriharikota on Friday night, boosting the NavIC constellation after a shortage of operational satellites. The rocket lifted off at 11.51pm and placed the 2,250kg satellite into orbit around 18 minutes later. Isro chairman V Narayanan said the launch restored NavIC's operation, which requires four satellites for positioning services. NVS-03 carries an indigenously developed atomic clock and adds a new L1 signal to improve civilian use.
items.title: Isro Successfully Launches NVS-03 Navigation Satellite

items.summary: The WTO's Global Review 2026 ended with a declaration on partnerships for trade and development, prepared by the Secretariat to aid public understanding. It recognises technical assistance as key for integrating least developed countries into global trade and calls for scaling up resources through grant, concessional and blended finance. WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala welcomed it as renewing the organisation brick by brick, while Peru's Committee on Trade and Development chair noted it is the first multilateral outcome on this topic after 20 years.
items.title: WTO Concludes Global Review With Trade-Development Declaration

items.summary: Inside Climate News reports that Texas, once the favored site for data centers, has become politically hostile to new projects. BaRupOn LLC built a 700-acre campus in East Texas after close state support, but by 2026 developers say the governor's office no longer responds to emails. Gov. Greg Abbott now orders audits of power and water use and pauses environmental permits until standards are met; Diode Ventures withdrew its Henderson County project as an example. Analysts at Aurora Energy Research track 277 gigawatts nationally, with only 81 gigawatts from proven operators like Meta and 145 gigawatts from newcomers. Beaufils expects speculative projects to disappear. The shift reflects community opposition and a tight Abbott reelection race against Gina Hinojosa.
items.title: Texas Data Center Boom Falters Amid Backlash and Abbott's Guardrails

items.summary: At a two-day summit concluded in Montreal, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the Alliance for the Future, describing it as the deepest possible partnership between Canada and the 27-member bloc. The leaders pledged that future discussions would create an integrated market worth tens of billions of dollars and reduce trade restrictions. As part of concluding talks, Canada agreed to contribute to a €90bn support loan for Ukraine. Carney also cited a planned merger between Cohere Inc and Germany’s Aleph Alpha GmbH as a step toward reducing reliance on American AI firms, with the Canadian government taking a stake worth up to C$1.6bn in the new company. A clearer scope of Canada’s associate membership would be defined at a 2027 summit.
items.title: Canada and EU Announce Alliance for the Future

items.summary: A tech stock sell-off began earlier this month and intensified with disappointing earnings from leading companies, driving US markets down by hundreds of billions Friday. The decline knocked nearly $1tn off the Nasdaq in one week and erased about $2tn in a month. Nvidia fell 3.1%, Intel dropped nearly 30%, Alphabet lost more than 12% after reporting heavy AI spending, and Amazon reported weaker profits amid higher costs as investors question whether massive AI investment will generate returns quickly enough.
items.title: Tech Earnings Losses Trigger Nearly $1tn US Market Drop

items.summary: Democratic Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola denied knowing about an alleged scheme that placed two men named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The claim follows a New York Times report alleging her campaign recruited spoiler candidates, which the BBC has not independently verified. Incumbent Republican Senator Dan S Sullivan and allies accuse Democrats of confusing voters.
items.title: Alaska Senate candidate denies knowledge of alleged ballot scheme

items.summary: Ian Thomas, chief executive of the City of London Corporation, has been named the most influential Black Briton in this year's Black Powerlist awards. The 57-year-old is the first Black person to lead the Square Mile's governing body in its more than 900-year history. He tops the 2027 list and takes second place behind Comfort Ero of the International Crisis Group.
items.title: City of London chief named top UK Black Briton

items.summary: The Maui Department of the Prosecuting Attorney is expected soon to have an investigator working full-time on contractor fraud cases targeting survivors of the 2023 Lahaina wildfire, county officials say. Mayor Richard Bissen asked County Council Chair Alice Lee to introduce legislation authorizing a seventh hire after reports rose; the council unanimously advanced it, with final passage expected Nov. 13. The move follows a joint Civil Beat and Inside Climate News investigation documenting survivors' problems with rebuild contractors. Prosecutor Andrew Martin said his office would assign an investigator full-time starting when a new deputy prosecutor begins work on Nov. 6, funded through cost savings rather than immediate budget cost.
items.title: Maui Prosecuting Attorney Adds Investigator for Wildfire Contractor Fraud
